# Footnotes

## Basic footnote

Here is a sentence with a footnote.[^1]

And another sentence with a different footnote.[^note]

[^1]: This is the content of footnote 1.

[^note]: This is a named footnote with a longer definition
    that spans multiple lines using indentation.

## Multiple references to the same footnote

The same footnote can be referenced multiple times.[^shared]

Here it is again.[^shared]

[^shared]: Shared footnote content referenced from two places.

## Footnote with formatting

Text with formatted footnote.[^formatted]

[^formatted]: This footnote contains **bold**, *italic*,
    `inline code`, and a [link](./file.md).

## Footnote with block content

Content referencing a complex footnote.[^complex]

[^complex]: This footnote has multiple paragraphs.

    Second paragraph of the same footnote, indented.

    - list item one
    - list item two

## Unused footnote definition

The following footnote is defined but never referenced.[^unused]

[^unused]: This definition has no reference in the document.

## Consecutive footnotes

Sentence with two footnotes at once.[^a][^b]

[^a]: First of the pair.

[^b]: Second of the pair.

## Final paragraph

Regular text after all footnotes.
